::: callout-note
## How to use this quiz

This quiz is designed as a **formative self-assessment tool**, not as a test.

Its purpose is to help you:
- check your understanding of the key concepts from Topic 4,
- identify which types of thinking you find more difficult, and
- guide your revision before the tutorial and future assessments.

### What this quiz measures

Each question belongs to one of four categories:

- **Subject Knowledge (SK):** definitions, concepts, and facts.  
- **Analysis (AN):** understanding relationships and economic mechanisms.  
- **Problem Solving (PS):** applying concepts to new situations.  
- **Mathematical Thinking (MT):** working with equations and quantitative relationships.

Your score will be broken down by category so you can see **where** you are strong and where you need more practice.

### How to complete the quiz

- You may use your notes and the lecture materials.
- Take your time — the goal is understanding, not speed.
- Use the **Hints** if you get stuck.
- You may refresh and retry the quiz as many times as you like.

### How to interpret your results

- A low score is **not a problem** — it tells you what to focus on.
- If you score low in:
  - **SK:** revise definitions and core concepts.
  - **AN:** revisit the logic of the models and examples.
  - **PS:** practise applying concepts to new cases.
  - **MT:** practise the mathematical calculations and equations.

### About the leaderboard

The leaderboard is optional and anonymous. It exists only to make practice more engaging.  
It has **no effect** on your grade and is not used for evaluation.

The only purpose of this quiz is to support your learning.

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(webexercises)
```

<!-- FEEDBACK SCRIPT: interactive quiz with self-assessment -->
```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  // 1) Configure your Google Apps Script Web App URL here.
  //    Example: https://script.google.com/macros/s/XXXXXXXXXXXX/exec
  const ENDPOINT = "https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbysCOTW2ZLw5ruYY84Y-o0zB7nt0jkowiC3OoKJSdh2OYv-ZXa_1vTb_TU4BYwcwSZ0Jw/exec";

  const norm = s => (s || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();

  function getSelectedLabelText(qEl) {
    const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
    if (!input) return "";
    const label = input.closest('label') || document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]');
    return label ? norm(label.textContent) : "";
  }

  function clearFeedback(qEl) {
    qEl.querySelectorAll("label").forEach(l => l.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect"));
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (line) {
      line.textContent = "";
      line.classList.add("hidden");
    }
  }

  function setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect) {
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (!line) return;
    line.textContent = isCorrect ? "Correct." : "Incorrect.";
    line.classList.remove("hidden");
  }

  async function postAttempt(payload) {
    // Do not attempt POST if ENDPOINT is not configured
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) return;

    try {
      await fetch(ENDPOINT, {
        method: "POST",
        mode: "no-cors",
        keepalive: true,
        body: JSON.stringify(payload)
      });
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn("Could not save attempt:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadLeaderboard(quizName) {
    const table = document.getElementById("leaderboard");
    if (!table) return;

    // If not configured, show a friendly message and stop.
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Leaderboard is not configured yet. Add your Apps Script URL in the page source.</td></tr>";
      return;
    }

    try {
      const res = await fetch(ENDPOINT, { method: "GET" });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + res.status);
      const rows = await res.json();

      // Filter for this quiz only (defensive: older rows may not have the fields)
      const filtered = (rows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

      // Keep best score per nickname
      const best = new Map();
      filtered.forEach(r => {
        const nick = String(r.nickname || "").trim();
        if (!nick) return;
        const score = Number(r.score);
        const total = Number(r.total);
        const ts = new Date(r.timestamp || 0).getTime();

        const prev = best.get(nick);
        if (!prev || score > prev.score || (score === prev.score && ts < prev.ts)) {
          best.set(nick, { nickname: nick, score, total, ts });
        }
      });

      const leaderboard = Array.from(best.values())
        .sort((a, b) => (b.score - a.score) || (a.ts - b.ts))
        .slice(0, 30);

      if (leaderboard.length === 0) {
        table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>No attempts recorded yet.</td></tr>";
      } else {
        table.innerHTML =
          "<tr><th>Rank</th><th>Nickname</th><th>Score</th></tr>" +
          leaderboard.map((r, i) =>
            "<tr><td>" + (i + 1) + "</td><td>" + String(r.nickname) + "</td><td>" + r.score + " / " + r.total + "</td></tr>"
          ).join("");
      }

      // Load and display question statistics
      await loadQuestionStats(quizName, rows);
    } catch (err) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Could not load leaderboard.</td></tr>";
      console.warn("Leaderboard error:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadQuestionStats(quizName, allRows) {
    const statsContainer = document.getElementById("question-stats");
    if (!statsContainer) return;

    // Filter for this quiz only
    const filtered = (allRows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

    console.log("=== DEBUGGING QUESTION STATS ===");
    console.log("Filtered rows count:", filtered.length);
    if (filtered.length > 0) {
      console.log("Sample row:", filtered[0]);
    }

    // Build a map of question index to identifier
    const questionIdentifiers = {};
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
      if (categoryMatch) {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];
      } else {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = "Q" + (idx + 1);
      }
    });

    console.log("Question identifiers map:", questionIdentifiers);

    // Count incorrect attempts per question
    const questionStats = {};
    filtered.forEach((row, rowIdx) => {
      let details = row.details || {};
      
      // If details is a string (JSON), parse it
      if (typeof details === "string") {
        try {
          details = JSON.parse(details);
          console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Parsed details from string`);
        } catch (e) {
          console.warn(`Row ${rowIdx} - Could not parse details:`, details);
          return;
        }
      }

      console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Processing details:`, details);

      Object.entries(details).forEach(([questionId, qData]) => {
        if (!questionStats[questionId]) {
          questionStats[questionId] = { incorrectCount: 0, totalCount: 0 };
        }
        
        questionStats[questionId].totalCount += 1;
        
        // Check if answer was incorrect (ok: 0 means incorrect)
        const isIncorrect = qData.ok === 0;
        if (isIncorrect) {
          questionStats[questionId].incorrectCount += 1;
        }
      });
    });

    console.log("\nFinal question stats:", questionStats);

    // Get top 10 most incorrect questions, sorted by incorrect count
    const sortedQuestions = Object.entries(questionStats)
      .map(([qKey, stats]) => ({
        qKey: qKey,
        incorrectCount: stats.incorrectCount,
        totalCount: stats.totalCount,
        incorrectRate: stats.totalCount > 0 ? (stats.incorrectCount / stats.totalCount * 100).toFixed(1) : 0
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => b.incorrectCount - a.incorrectCount)
      .slice(0, 10);

    console.log("Sorted questions:", sortedQuestions);

    if (sortedQuestions.length === 0) {
      statsContainer.innerHTML = "<p>No question statistics available yet.</p>";
    } else {
      statsContainer.innerHTML =
        "<h4>Top 10 Questions with Most Incorrect Attempts</h4>" +
        "<table style='width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse;'>" +
        "<tr style='border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;'><th style='text-align: left; padding: 8px;'>Question</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Total Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Rate</th></tr>" +
        sortedQuestions.map(q =>
          "<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>" +
          "<td style='padding: 8px;'>" + String(q.qKey) + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.totalCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectRate + "%</td>" +
          "</tr>"
        ).join("") +
        "</table>";
    }
  }

  async function submitQuiz() {
    const nicknameEl = document.getElementById("nickname");
    const resultEl = document.getElementById("quiz-result");
    const submitBtn = document.getElementById("quiz-submit");

    const nickname = (nicknameEl?.value || "").trim();
    if (!nickname) {
      alert("Please enter a nickname before submitting.");
      nicknameEl?.focus();
      return;
    }

    // Lock submit to avoid double posting
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;

    let score = 0;
    let total = 0;
    const details = {};
    
    // Category scores
    const categories = {
      SK: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Subject Knowledge" },
      AN: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Analysis" },
      PS: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Problem Solving" },
      MT: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Mathematical Thinking" }
    };

    const questions = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q"));

    // Clear any prior feedback first (important if student re-submits)
    questions.forEach(clearFeedback);

    questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      total += 1;
      const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
      const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
      const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);

      const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
      if (isCorrect) score += 1;

      // Extract category and question ID from question text (SK1, AN1, PS1, MT1, etc.)
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
      let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);
      
      if (categoryMatch) {
        const cat = categoryMatch[1];
        const num = categoryMatch[2];
        questionId = cat + num;
        
        categories[cat].total += 1;
        if (isCorrect) categories[cat].score += 1;
      }

      details[questionId] = { selected, correct, ok: isCorrect ? 1 : 0 };

      // Mark only after submit
      if (selected) {
        const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
        const label = input?.closest("label") || (input ? document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]') : null);
        if (label) label.classList.add(isCorrect ? "is-correct" : "is-incorrect");
      }
      setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect);
    });

    if (resultEl) {
      let resultHTML = "<strong>Overall Score: " + score + " / " + total + "</strong><br><br>";
      
      // Add category breakdown
      for (const key in categories) {
        const cat = categories[key];
        if (cat.total > 0) {
          resultHTML += cat.name + ": " + cat.score + " / " + cat.total + "<br>";
        }
      }
      
      // Add correct and incorrect questions
      const correctQuestions = [];
      const incorrectQuestions = [];
      
      questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
        const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
        const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
        const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);
        const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
        
        // Extract question ID from question text
        const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
        const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
        let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);
        if (categoryMatch) {
          questionId = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];
        }
        
        if (selected) {
          if (isCorrect) {
            correctQuestions.push(questionId);
          } else {
            incorrectQuestions.push(questionId);
          }
        }
      });
      
      resultHTML += "<br><strong>Correct Questions:</strong> " + (correctQuestions.length > 0 ? correctQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      resultHTML += "<strong>Incorrect Questions:</strong> " + (incorrectQuestions.length > 0 ? incorrectQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      
      resultEl.innerHTML = resultHTML;
    }

    // Persist attempt (best practice: store what you need; nickname only = low GDPR footprint)
    await postAttempt({
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      nickname,
      quiz: "Topic4",
      score,
      total,
      details
    });

    // Refresh leaderboard after a successful submit (or best-effort submit)
    await loadLeaderboard("Topic4");

    // Disable all radio buttons and submit button to prevent further changes
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q input[type='radio']").forEach(input => {
      input.disabled = true;
    });
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;
  }

  // Expose submitQuiz globally for the button onclick
  window.submitQuiz = submitQuiz;

  // Add a feedback line container to each question if it doesn't exist
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach(qEl => {
      if (!qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line")) {
        const line = document.createElement("div");
        line.className = "quiz-feedback-line hidden";
        qEl.appendChild(line);
      }
    });

    loadLeaderboard("Topic4");
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Subject Knowledge

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK1) In the quantity theory identity ($MV = PY$), what does $V$ represent?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "The velocity of money", "The value of real output", "The nominal interest rate", "Government spending"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The velocity of money"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Recall that the identity links money to nominal spending through how frequently money circulates.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK2) According to the monetarist long-run benchmark, a permanent increase in the level of money primarily affects:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Real output", "Employment", answer = "The price level", "The natural rate of unemployment"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The price level"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply the principle of long-run neutrality in the classical dichotomy.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK3) In the canonical monetarist model, equilibrium employment ($N^*$) is determined in the:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Money market", answer = "Labour market", "Goods market", "Government sector"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Labour market"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Identify which block determines real wages and employment before nominal variables are considered.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK4) The Fisher equation links the nominal interest rate ($i$) to:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Real money balances and output", "Government spending and taxes", answer = "The real interest rate and expected inflation", "Velocity and inflation"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The real interest rate and expected inflation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Distinguish between real returns and inflation compensation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK5) Money is described as "neutral" in the long run because changes in money:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Affect real output permanently", answer = "Affect only nominal variables permanently", "Eliminate unemployment", "Stabilise velocity automatically"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Affect only nominal variables permanently"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the classical dichotomy to separate real and nominal variables.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK6) Under stable velocity and constant real output growth, a higher permanent money growth rate implies:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Lower inflation", "Higher real growth", answer = "Higher long-run inflation", "Lower nominal interest rates"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Higher long-run inflation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Start from $MV=PY$ and consider growth rates.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK7) The natural-rate hypothesis implies that attempts to keep unemployment below $u^*$:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Permanently reduce unemployment", answer = "Cause accelerating inflation", "Lower expected inflation", "Reduce velocity"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Cause accelerating inflation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Think about how expectations adjust in the Phillips curve framework.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK8) Hyperinflation, under the Cagan criterion, begins when monthly inflation exceeds:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("10%", "25%", answer = "50%", "100%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="50%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Recall the numerical threshold used in historical classifications.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK9) In the Cagan money demand specification, higher expected inflation leads to:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Higher real money demand", answer = "Lower real money demand", "Higher real output", "Lower nominal interest rates"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Lower real money demand"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider how inflation expectations affect the opportunity cost of holding money.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK10) The constant money-growth ($k\%$) rule is motivated primarily by concerns about:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Fiscal deficits", answer = "Long and variable policy lags", "Labour supply elasticity", "Exchange-rate targeting"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Long and variable policy lags"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Focus on the critique of discretionary fine-tuning.</details>
</div>

## Analysis

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN1) If velocity becomes unstable due to financial innovation, which monetarist proposition is most directly weakened?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Long-run neutrality of money", "The Fisher effect", answer = "A stable link between money growth and nominal GDP growth", "The existence of unemployment"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="A stable link between money growth and nominal GDP growth"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Identify which empirical assumption connects money growth predictably to spending.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN2) Suppose prices adjust fully but nominal wages remain fixed temporarily after a monetary expansion. What happens to the real wage ($w/P$)?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It rises", answer = "It falls", "It remains unchanged", "It becomes indeterminate"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It falls"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Compare the speed of adjustment between numerator and denominator.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN3) Why does the expectations-augmented Phillips curve imply no permanent inflation-unemployment trade-off?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because velocity is constant", answer = "Because expected inflation adjusts over time", "Because money demand is fixed", "Because fiscal policy dominates"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because expected inflation adjusts over time"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider how adaptive expectations change the position of the short-run curve.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN4) If expected inflation rises permanently while the real interest rate is unchanged in the long run, what must happen to the nominal interest rate?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It falls", "It stays constant", answer = "It rises one-for-one", "It becomes negative"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It rises one-for-one"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply the Fisher relation carefully.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN5) A central bank increases money growth, but velocity simultaneously falls sharply during a crisis. What is the most likely short-run effect on inflation?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Inflation rises proportionately", "Inflation falls mechanically", answer = "The effect on inflation is ambiguous", "Inflation must accelerate"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The effect on inflation is ambiguous"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the identity $MV=PY$ and allow both components to change.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN6) In the monetarist four-block model, which adjustment restores long-run equilibrium after a monetary shock?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Permanent change in employment", "Permanent fall in real wages", answer = "Adjustment of nominal wages and prices", "Collapse of money demand"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Adjustment of nominal wages and prices"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Distinguish between real equilibrium determination and nominal adjustment.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN7) Why might money-growth targeting become impractical even if long-run neutrality holds?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because real output is unstable", answer = "Because velocity may shift unpredictably", "Because inflation is always zero", "Because unemployment disappears"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because velocity may shift unpredictably"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Separate theoretical neutrality from empirical stability of money demand.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN8) At the effective lower bound, why can QE still reduce longer-term yields?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("By permanently increasing real output", answer = "By lowering term and risk premia", "By eliminating inflation expectations", "By fixing velocity"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="By lowering term and risk premia"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Think in terms of portfolio-balance mechanisms.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN9) In a high-inflation environment, raising inflation further may generate less seigniorage revenue because:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Government spending falls", answer = "Real money balances shrink", "Output rises sharply", "Interest rates fall"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Real money balances shrink"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider how the inflation tax base responds to higher expected inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN10) Why does the natural-rate hypothesis undermine activist stabilization aimed at permanently lowering unemployment?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because fiscal policy is stronger", "Because real wages are irrelevant", answer = "Because expectations adapt and shift the Phillips curve", "Because money demand vanishes"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because expectations adapt and shift the Phillips curve"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Focus on dynamic expectation adjustment rather than static correlations.</details>
</div>

## Problem Solving

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS1) A country increases its money supply permanently. In the short run, workers suffer from money illusion and underestimate inflation. What is the most likely temporary outcome?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Higher real wages and lower output", answer = "Lower perceived real wages and higher employment", "Immediate return to equilibrium", "Permanent fall in unemployment"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Lower perceived real wages and higher employment"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider how misperceptions affect labour demand decisions.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS2) Suppose money growth rises from 4% to 8% while real output growth remains at 2% and velocity is stable. What happens to long-run inflation?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "It rises from 2% to 6%", "It falls to 0%", "It stays at 2%", "It becomes negative"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It rises from 2% to 6%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the growth-rate version of the quantity equation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS3) During a crisis, the central bank doubles money growth, but households sharply increase liquidity preference. Inflation remains low. Which explanation fits monetarist logic?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Money no longer matters", answer = "Velocity has fallen significantly", "The natural rate has disappeared", "Real output must have doubled"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Velocity has fallen significantly"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Separate money supply changes from spending behaviour.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS4) Expected inflation increases by 3 percentage points. If the real interest rate is unchanged, what happens to the nominal rate?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "It rises by 3 percentage points", "It falls by 3 percentage points", "It is unchanged", "It becomes zero"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It rises by 3 percentage points"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply the Fisher equation directly.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS5) A government finances persistent deficits through money creation. Expected inflation rises sharply, and real money balances collapse. What risk emerges?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Stable disinflation", answer = "Hyperinflation dynamics", "Permanent rise in real output", "Declining nominal interest rates"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Hyperinflation dynamics"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider nonlinear effects in money demand.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS6) If unemployment is pushed below $u^*$ through expansionary policy, what must occur over time to restore equilibrium?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Expected inflation falls", answer = "Expected inflation rises", "Real wages permanently decline", "Velocity stabilises"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Expected inflation rises"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Trace the implications of adaptive expectations.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS7) A permanent increase in money growth raises inflation expectations immediately. What happens to real output in the long run?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It increases permanently", "It decreases permanently", answer = "It returns to its supply-determined level", "It becomes unpredictable"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It returns to its supply-determined level"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Recall super-neutrality in the benchmark model.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS8) If velocity falls persistently while money growth is constant, what must happen to inflation in the long run (holding real growth constant)?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It rises", answer = "It falls", "It is unaffected", "It becomes hyperinflationary"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It falls"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Work with growth rates in the quantity identity.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS9) A credible fiscal reform eliminates expected future monetisation of deficits. What is the likely immediate effect on expected inflation?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It rises", answer = "It falls", "It remains unchanged", "It doubles"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It falls"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Expectations respond to regime credibility.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS10) Why might a central bank prefer a rule over discretion in the presence of long and variable lags?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("To eliminate unemployment", answer = "To stabilise expectations and reduce policy-induced volatility", "To increase velocity", "To fix the real interest rate permanently"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="To stabilise expectations and reduce policy-induced volatility"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Focus on informational limits and transmission delays.</details>
</div>

## Mathematical Thinking

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT1) Given $MV = PY$, if $M=100$, $V=5$, and $Y=250$, what is $P$?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("1", answer = "2", "5", "10"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="2"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Rearrange the identity to isolate the price level.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT2) If money growth $\mu = 6\%$ and real output growth $g = 2\%$, with stable velocity, inflation $\pi$ is approximately:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("2%", answer = "4%", "6%", "8%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="4%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use $\pi \approx \mu - g$.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT3) From $P = \frac{M}{kY^s}$, if $M$ doubles while $k$ and $Y^s$ are constant, $P$:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Halves", answer = "Doubles", "Is unchanged", "Falls to zero"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Doubles"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Identify proportional relationships.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT4) Using $i \approx r + \pi^e$, if $r=2\%$ and $\pi^e=5\%$, then $i$ equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("3%", "5%", answer = "7%", "10%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="7%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Add real return and expected inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT5) In $\pi_t = \pi_t^e - \alpha(u_t - u^*)$, if $u_t = u^*$, then inflation equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Zero", answer = "Expected inflation", "Negative inflation", "The real rate"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Expected inflation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Substitute carefully when the unemployment gap is zero.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT6) If real money demand follows $\frac{M}{P} = A e^{-\alpha \pi^e}$, what happens to $\frac{M}{P}$ when $\pi^e$ rises?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It increases exponentially", answer = "It decreases exponentially", "It stays constant", "It becomes linear"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It decreases exponentially"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider the sign in the exponent.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT7) If $\mu = 10\%$, $g=3\%$, and velocity growth is 2%, inflation equals approximately:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("5%", "7%", answer = "9%", "15%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="9%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use growth accounting: $\mu + v = \pi + g$.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT8) If $u^* = 5\%$, $u_t=3\%$, $\alpha=0.5$, and $\pi_t^e=4\%$, what is $\pi_t$ (ignoring shocks)?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("3%", "4%", answer = "5%", "6%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="5%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Compute the unemployment gap first.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT9) If seigniorage revenue is $S = \pi \cdot \frac{M}{P}$ and real balances fall as inflation rises, the relationship between $S$ and $\pi$ is most likely:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Strictly linear", "Downward sloping", answer = "Hump-shaped", "Vertical"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Hump-shaped"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Combine the inflation tax rate with a shrinking tax base.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT10) If expected inflation rises by 4 percentage points and nominal rates rise by 4 percentage points while real rates remain unchanged, this empirical pattern supports:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Liquidity trap theory", answer = "Fisher effect", "Super-neutrality failure", "Velocity instability"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Fisher effect"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Look for one-for-one adjustment between inflation expectations and nominal rates.</details>
</div>
